evasoes.descricao: Semantic rewording of the hostile request using synonyms, circumlocutions, metaphors or indirect language to evade keyword-based filters while keeping the meaning intact.

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251, data/defesas.json): paraphrase is not covered by lexical matching, which judges surface and not intent.

evasoes.descricao: Encodes the payload with classic ciphers (ROT13, Caesar, Base64, Morse, A1Z26, ASCII hex, etc.) or asks the model to decode before answering, bypassing filters that operate on plain text.

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251, data/defesas.json): payload encoding falls outside the fuzzy heuristic, which only catches anagrams.

evasoes.descricao: Translates the payload into a low-resource language or one less represented in safety training, exploiting the fact that safety alignment is weaker in non-English languages.

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251, data/defesas.json): payload translation is not covered by lexical matching.

evasoes.descricao: Uses Unicode homoglyphs, diacritics, invisible (zero-width) characters, font variation (Unicode bold/italic) or markdown/HTML formatting to disguise keywords and evade textual detection.

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251): lexical matching does not cover encoding/obfuscation beyond anagrams; the item's sources do not test Unicode.

evasoes.descricao: Splits the hostile payload into harmless fragments distributed across the prompt or across turns, instructing the model to concatenate them to rebuild the full instruction.
Applies deterministic rule-based transformations (Pig Latin, Leetspeak, reversed words, word-level permutation, custom cipher) that the model can reverse internally.

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251): paraphrase or encoding are not covered by lexical matching; R72 and R100 do not test a lexical filter.

evasoes.descricao: Uses an auxiliary LLM to automatically generate payload variations that preserve meaning but avoid detection, including genetic algorithms over prompts (AutoDAN, GPTFUZZER, TAP).

bypass.nota: Documented weakness of D01 (R251): payload paraphrase is not covered by lexical matching; the sources read do not test AutoDAN against a lexical filter.

evasoes.descricao: Exploits tokenizer quirks (compound tokens, glitch tokens, boundary splitting) to create text representations that look harmless at the character level but yield tokens the model interprets differently.

bypass.nota: R18 §III: single word 'hardest to be detected' by filters or pattern matching; no experiment (§V.C).

evasoes.descricao: Applies intentional misspellings, scrambling of inner letters (keeping the first and last letters) or abbreviations that humans and LLMs understand but exact-match filters miss.

bypass.nota: R251 (OWASP): the typoglycemia attack, with scrambled inner letters and correct first and last letters, bypasses keyword-based filters; guide claim, no measurement.

evasoes.descricao: Embeds the hostile instruction in an alternative modality (image with text, audio, PDF document, video) that the model processes but text filters do not inspect.

bypass.nota: R35: the review reports that hiding the malicious content in the visual modality makes the model derive the context without noticing anything malicious, due to the lack of cross-modality alignment; report of third-party work, no figures.

evasoes.descricao: Defines a bijective mapping (custom alphabet, invented language, substitution dictionary) between words/characters and their equivalents, encoding the hostile instruction in that mapping and asking the model to decode it.

bypass.nota: Weakness in defesas.json: payload encoding is not covered by lexical matching (R251).

evasoes.descricao: Hides the hostile instruction using textual steganographic techniques: first letters of each line (acrostic), variable spacing, bold/italic marking, or encoding in image/document metadata.
